source: Original personal hero scenes and canonical Case002 art storyboard: HJ01 and HF01 accepted as separate one-image-per-turn hero-gap candidates; five personal illustrations still pending.

scenes.focus: a broad-shouldered private detective in a rain-dark overcoat stands with his back to the viewer in a tense quiet exchange with a weary mustached private railway watchman who lowers his eyes instead of challenging him
scenes.camera: intimate vertical over-the-shoulder view from behind the detective on the right; watchman under the oil lantern on the left and the wet rail siding and lock gate receding in the fog
scenes.location: an old canal lock beside the private industrial railway siding and a timber guard booth in Birmingham in the 1920s
required: one silent broad-shouldered detective in a dark soaked overcoat and flat cap viewed from behind, no identifiable facial features
one weary mustached railway watchman in a period uniform coat and service cap looking down, his rifle safely slung across the shoulder
one illuminated old wooden guard booth, wet rail siding, cold canal water and a weathered timber lock gate in one continuous space
scenes.background: wet cobbles and railway rails curving past the guard booth, a canal-lock wheel and gate, soot-dark factories and smoking chimneys fading into industrial mist
scenes.light: warm lantern light on the watchman's downturned face and damp wooden booth, contrasting with cold blue-grey night fog on the canal and rails
scenes.npc: Jack is visible only from behind and cannot be mistaken for a new protagonist; the unnamed railway guard is seen in guarded three-quarter view, no additional participants
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: This character-specific confrontation occurs before the outcome of the player's decision. Neither a threat nor Jack's reference to Hale has necessarily gained the passage. Guard's averted gaze is hesitation, not a signed confession, a completed bribe, a physical attack or an earned witness statement. Jack's face remains unestablished and his chosen identity is preserved.
avoid: identifiable portrait of Jack or invented close-up face, additional civilian or Tommy appearing at the gate
the watchman pointing, firing or swinging the rifle at anyone, a fight or visible injury
an open unlocked gate, the detective already granted passage or a written guard confession
readable railway timetable, fabricated stamped evidence or an anachronistic modern security booth

scenes.focus: an observant man in a heavy rain-dark wool coat and tweed cap pauses on a steep narrow exterior iron staircase, his face concealed as he looks through an open freight-office window at shipping documents illuminated by a desk lamp
scenes.camera: vertical close-medium composition from behind the detective at stair level, a diagonal iron railing in the foreground and an open wooden-paned window leading the eye into the desk inside
scenes.location: the second-storey back wall of a late-night 1920s Birmingham private railway freight office beside a dark industrial siding
required: one man in a dark wool coat and flat cap with only the back of his head and hand on a wet iron railing visible
one open weathered wooden window above the narrow outdoor metal steps, with raindrops catching the light
one period office desk inside with a closed leather ledger, a single loose shipping paper, an inkstand and pigeonhole files
scenes.background: damp brickwork, black wrought-iron stairs, old railway wagons and wet tracks receding toward factory smokestacks under a smoky night sky
scenes.light: a warm desk lamp inside the office contrasts with cold blue-grey rain and a few distant amber railway lamps
scenes.npc: only the anonymous rear-view detective on the stairs; no other person is identifiable
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: Finn is using an opportunistic open window and exterior stairs to learn where a clean copy of the shipping ledger may be found. He is not shown stealing it, entering by force, opening any safe, acquiring the original document or proving which clerk forged it. The selected hero's approved facial appearance must not be invented.
avoid: Finn's identifiable face, a substituted player portrait, a uniformed second person at the window
bent safe door, picklock, broken window, forced entry or destroyed office furniture
shipping papers with readable false names, invented dates, forged signatures or a completed proof of guilt
an original ledger already in Finn's possession, a heroic getaway or discovered alarm
